title: Network Security Architecture: Segmentation, Defense in Depth and Zero Trust

header.html: 4.2 Understand network security architecture: Comprehending network segmentation (for example firewall zones, Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN), micro-segmentation); Defense in Depth; Zero Trust (ZT)
the official ISC2 CC exam outline

html:
1Network segmentation

Segmentation divides a network into smaller zones so that a breach in one zone does not spread everywhere. It also lets you apply different rules to each zone.

Technique How it divides Note
Firewall zones Firewalls separate trust levels Internet, DMZ, internal, restricted
DMZ (screened subnet) A buffer zone for public-facing servers If a web server falls, the internal network is still behind another firewall
VLAN A logical network on shared switches Separates departments, guests, voice
Micro-segmentation Fine-grained rules around each workload or application, often in software Stops lateral movement inside a data center or cloud
Physical separation (air gap) No connection at all Highest isolation, used for the most sensitive systems
Exam tip

. Public servers go in the DMZ. A VLAN separates groups; micro-segmentation protects individual workloads. Segmentation limits the blast radius.

2Defense in depth

Defense in depth uses several layers of different controls, so that if one fails, others still protect. No single control is trusted alone.

Layer Example controls
Policies and awareness Policies, training
Physical Locks, badges, cameras
Perimeter Firewalls, DMZ, email filtering
Network Segmentation, IDS and IPS
Host / endpoint Patching, antivirus, hardening
Application Secure coding, WAF
Data Encryption, backups, access control
Identity MFA, least privilege

Defense in depth combines technical, administrative and physical controls (Module 4) and preventive, detective and corrective functions.

Exam tip

. Defense in depth = layers. Layers should be different, because two controls of the same kind can fail the same way.

3Zero trust

Zero trust (ZT) drops the idea that the inside of the network is trusted. No user, device or network location is trusted automatically.

Principle Meaning
Never trust, always verify Every request is authenticated and authorized
Least privilege Minimum access, often just in time
Assume breach Design as if an attacker is already inside; segment and monitor
Verify explicitly Use identity, device health, location, behavior for every decision
Micro-segmentation Small trust zones around resources
Continuous monitoring Re-check during the session, not only at login
Traditional (castle and moat) Zero trust
Strong perimeter, trusted inside No implicit trust anywhere
Access by network location Access by identity and context
VPN gives broad access Per-application, per-request access

AI helps by separating AI development from production data with segmentation and by spotting anomalies.

Exam tip

. Zero trust: never trust, always verify, assume breach, least privilege. A VPN alone is not zero trust.

4Other architecture ideas

Idea Meaning
Network access control (NAC) Checks a device before it joins (patched, approved)
Honeypot A decoy system that attracts attackers so you can study them
Bastion host / jump server A hardened gateway for administrator access

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A company hosts a public web server and wants it separated from the internal network by a buffer zone. Which design is this?

  • AA VLAN that mixes web and office traffic
  • BA DMZ, also called a screened subnet
  • CAn air gap with no network connection
  • DA flat network with a single firewall rule
Show the answer

Answer: B. A DMZ is a buffer zone for public-facing servers between the internet and the internal network.

S2A data center wants to stop an attacker who is already inside from moving between application servers. Which technique helps most?

  • AMicro-segmentation with rules for each workload
  • BA stronger password policy for the guests
  • CA bigger firewall at the internet edge
  • DA DMZ for the print servers
Show the answer

Answer: A. Micro-segmentation applies fine-grained rules between workloads and limits lateral movement.

S3A company uses a firewall, MFA, encryption, endpoint protection and staff training together. Which concept is this?

  • AZero trust, which verifies every request
  • BDefense in depth, which uses many layers
  • CSeparation of duties, which splits tasks
  • DLeast privilege, which limits access
Show the answer

Answer: B. Using several different layers of control is defense in depth.

S4Which statement best describes zero trust?

  • ANo user or device is trusted until verified for each request
  • BUsers inside the office network are trusted by default
  • CA VPN login gives full trust to the connected user
  • DOnly the perimeter firewall needs strong protection
Show the answer

Answer: A. Zero trust means never trust, always verify, for every request and not only at the perimeter.

S5Which controls make defense in depth stronger?

  • ADifferent kinds of controls at different layers
  • BSeveral copies of the same type of control
  • COne very strong control at the network perimeter
  • DRemoving controls that overlap each other
Show the answer

Answer: A. Layers should differ so that one failure mode does not defeat them all.

S6A guest Wi-Fi network must not reach the finance systems on the same switches. Which feature separates them?

  • AA single shared VLAN for all users
  • BA longer Wi-Fi passphrase for the guests
  • CA larger IP address range for the switch
  • DSeparate VLANs with firewall rules between them
Show the answer

Answer: D. VLANs separate groups logically, and firewall rules control any traffic between them.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What does a DMZ hold?

Show the answer

Public-facing servers, in a buffer zone.

R2What does segmentation limit?

Show the answer

The spread of a breach, the blast radius.

R3What is the core idea of zero trust?

Show the answer

Never trust, always verify.

R4What does assume breach mean?

Show the answer

Design as if an attacker is already inside.

R5What is defense in depth?

Show the answer

Several different layers of controls.

R6What does a honeypot do?

Show the answer

Attracts attackers as a decoy so they can be studied.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Segmentation firewall zones, DMZ, VLAN, micro-segmentation, air gap; limits blast radius
Defense in depth many different layers: policy, physical, perimeter, network, host, app, data, identity
Zero trust never trust, always verify; least privilege; assume breach; continuous monitoring
Extras NAC, honeypot, jump server
